findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves. On what and why, the page does its job straight away.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: what you need first, how to clone, how to install, and a one-line first command. A link at the top jumps straight to them, so 'what to do next' is well covered.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The opening promises that each commit can be traced to its models, cost and verdict, but the section meant to show that prints an error instead. It is the second thing a newcomer reads, and it suggests the showcase is broken.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets a page whose title and most of whose content are about another tool, firstmate. Only three paragraphs at the top and the Next steps section describe Athena itself.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The middle of the page is a detailed state machine with heavy jargon such as places-held, close-pending, stale wake and exit 75. A newcomer is unlikely to read it and gets no short summary of what it proves about Athena.
findings.source: Transitions, cards t1–t12 (e.g. "Guard: worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward...")

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is not defined. That is honest, but it leaves a newcomer holding words they cannot fully understand.
findings.source: Glossary: "captain call — The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (also durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)

findings.text: This link sits in the opening section and is aimed at the site's owner, not a visitor. A newcomer may not know whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The page explains its citation scheme, and every claim links to exact lines at a fixed commit. A curious reader can see what Athena's 'traceable' promise looks like in practice.
findings.source: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end."

findings.text: This closing note describes Athena's internal layout and gives a newcomer nothing they can use.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
